Resolves #19186

A committed cross-popup conversion now says what its dispose did. The engine transaction's dispose effect (`NativeVesselTransaction.effectsFor().disposeVessel`) publishes a `dispose` receipt before the first retire call and amends it in place — `attempts`, `admitted`, the refusal class (`no-vessel` · `identity-mismatch` · `host-close-refused` · `vessel-replaced`) and whether the vessel's window was still alive when the close was refused — through the same `publishReceipt(key, receipt)` seam the park and restore receipts ride; the Workstation and Demo B map the third key to `lastVesselDisposeReceipt`. A close the host refused while the window still exists is retried exactly once after a macrotask, and the retry is bound to the lineage the first call addressed: every retire call carries the registry's generation token, `TearOut.retireActiveVessel` refuses a superseded token, and the effect re-reads the registry after the macrotask — an entry gone ends as `no-vessel`, a different window or token as `vessel-replaced`, never a close (round 1). A window already gone, a missing entry or a mismatched name is never retried, so the park machine's one-call contract and the "never close twice" rule both hold. `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL`'s pointer-path commit arms read the receipt over the Neural Link beside the closure they already asserted (the native title-bar arms keep their closure assertion on `lastTearOutClose`) — the same read the operator's hand run makes.

Evidence: L1 (the transaction's eight dispose arms + the TearOut lineage arm, the park machine, the Workstation and Demo B unit tiers) → L2 achieved headless (`WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL`'s pointer-path commit arms read `admitted: true`, one attempt, over the Neural Link; the native title-bar arms assert closure separately) → L3 required for AC-2's hand clause and AC-4's regression question (the operator's display). Residual: AC-2 (the hand read) and AC-4 (regressed or pre-existing), Residual-Owner: #19101 (my open Dock Layouts + Workstation survey; the post-merge item is recorded there).

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline `pr-body` + `substrate-size` run in CI. ticket-intake: self-authored in an earlier session — drift probe over the ticket's named paths since the re-scope: empty intersection; prescription checked: `src/dashboard/dock/window/NativeVesselTransaction.mjs` — owns the concern (the dispose effect already resolves the host's registry entry, calls the host's retire seam and publishes the park / restore receipts; `VesselPark` keeps its exactly-once terminal, the hosts map one key).

## Deltas from ticket
- The receipt and the retry live in the engine transaction's dispose effect, not on the host and not in `VesselPark`: the effect already resolves the host's registry entry and publishes the park / restore receipts, so the hosts map one more key and the park machine's exactly-once terminal is untouched. The refusal classes are the registry's view (entry present, name matches); the tear-out's private slot stays private.
- The ticket's witness premise was stale and is corrected in its body as the author: the native commit poll already expected `sourceClosed: true`, and Demo B's commit arm transfers from the main window, so it has no source vessel to close. AC-3 is the receipt assertion beside the closure, plus both other suites at baseline.
- The receipt is the POINTER path's: the native title-bar path disposes through the Workstation's returned-vessel retirement (`retireReturnedVessel` → `NativeVesselTransaction.closeVessel`, which publishes `lastTearOutClose`), not through the park transaction's dispose effect — the native witnesses read `null` for the new member and taught it. The 2026-09-26 sighting was a hand pointer drag, so the receipt sits where the sighting lives; AC-2 says so now.
- The retry waits one macrotask, not "after the terminal settles": the dispose runs inside the park machine's terminal, so the terminal cannot settle before it returns; one macrotask is what lets a settle still in flight land.

## Test Evidence
Headless e2e, outside CI (the Workstation witnesses are selected only with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`): `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` 2 passed / 2 failed at the head — the two small-over-large commit arms green WITH the receipt assertion (`admitted: true, attempts: 1, stage: 'retired'` read through `app.getComponent`), the two large-over-small arms red on "target proxy width follows the live source viewport" exactly as on dev (#19297, Ada's); `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` 3 of 3 green (closure asserted; the member reads `null` on that path, which is why the receipt assertion moved); `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL`: 3 failed at the head AND on dev's own files — control run with `DemoBWorkspace.mjs` and `NativeVesselTransaction.mjs` checked out from `origin/dev`, the same three arms with the same errors ("the CDP adapter must place the real moving vessel over the observed target", "Target page, context or browser has been closed") — dev's headless baseline on this host, not this branch.
AC-4: no survivor reproduced headless at the head (the pointer-path arms' receipts read `admitted: true, attempts: 1` on every committed conversion; the native title-bar arms assert closure through `lastTearOutClose`); the hand run's receipt decides the regression question (#19101).
